reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports all key premises: E1 describes the activated sintering mechanism and continuous Cu network formation, while E2 reports the exact thermal conductivity enhancement (24.3%) and processing conditions for the 0.8 wt.% Cu@Gr composite. The representation of the baseline conductivity (~264 W/(m·K)) is slightly imprecise, as E2 states this value for the doped composite, not the undoped baseline, but the overall support is strong.
premises: Graphene enhances activated sintering of W–Cu by increasing grain boundary diffusivity of W
Cu@Gr promotes formation of a continuous Cu network and high relative density
Cu@Gr partially prevents formation of WC at the interface
0.8 wt.% Cu@Gr addition yields ~24% thermal conductivity enhancement over undoped W–Cu
SPS at 1280 °C, 30 MPa, 10 min is a suitable processing window for Cu@Gr/W–Cu composites
